one_month_reasoning: The window holds three scheduled events. (1) ASML Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-14 at 07:00 CET (confirmed on ASML IR). Guidance is EUR 11.0-12.0B sales at 55-57% GM; consensus is EUR 10.65 EPS on EUR 11.68B, inside the guide, so the swing factor is the first qualitative 2027 view. The Q2 call supports a constructive one: 2027 low-NA EUV is 'close to fully covered', capacity rises ~30% to ~85 units, and a further ~30% for 2028 is under study. Bookings are no longer disclosed. (2) TSMC Q3 results on about 2026-10-15, a capex read-across. (3) The late-October FOMC after the 2026-09-16 hike to 3.75-4.00%. The statement and dots point to one more hike in 2026, which the market mostly places in December, so the October risk is small. The supervisor's check, which I verified, rules out a MATCH Act outcome inside the window: the Senate adjourned 2026-09-30 and returns the week of 11-09, S.4281 has had no Banking Committee markup, and the realistic path is a December conference text. Against an upside call: the stock has already bounced ~15% from the $1,575.15 close of 2026-09-14, and consensus 2027 EPS has already risen ~25% in 90 days. Micron's 2026-09-30 guide and TrendForce's Q4 DRAM price rises are positive but already public. With no directional edge, I use a lognormal centred at about $1,814 with 14% monthly sigma (a little above 46%/3.5 = 13% because of the earnings print).

fair_value.method: This is a 60/40 blend of a forward P/E and a 2028E FCF yield, both converted at EUR/USD 1.1243. The P/E leg is NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of EUR 58.3 ($65.5) x 27.5 = $1,803. The FCF leg is 2028E FCF/share of EUR 54.5 at a 3.35% yield = EUR 1,625, or $1,827. 2028E EPS is EUR 60.5, anchored on consensus 2028 sales of EUR 65.0B at a 36.5% net margin on ~378M shares (EUR 62.7), less a 3.5% probability-weighted MATCH Act haircut.

inputs_detail.derivation: Alpha Spread consensus is EUR 51.72 and MarketScreener's is EUR 52.29 (2027 sales EUR 54.6B, NI EUR 19.5B). The supervisor confirmed it is in EUR. The Q2 transcript backs it: ~30% more low-NA units (~65 to ~85) and an E/F mix worth ~45% more wafer capacity (sources 2, 11).
H1 reported EUR 14.74. Q3 at the guide midpoint gives ~EUR 10.5 and the implied Q4 of ~EUR 14.4B sales gives ~EUR 13.9, for ~EUR 39. That matches MarketScreener's EUR 38.58.

MarketScreener consensus (42 analysts) is EUR 64.99B, +19% on 2027. That is consistent with management studying another ~30% low-NA capacity step for 2028 (source 2) and with TSMC's 'even more significantly higher' three-year capex (source 13). I take consensus rather than my round-1 judgment, as the supervisor asked.

Consensus net margins are 35.7% for 2027 and 37.5% for 2028. I use 36.5%, below the 2028 consensus, because Q3 GM is guided at 55-57% (source 1) and the 2030 model's 56-60% GM range (source 6) only reaches 37%+ net at the upper half.

Q2-26 basic weighted shares were 384.5M (source 3). The EUR 12B 2026-28 buyback (source 5) runs at ~EUR 1.1B a quarter (Q2, source 1). Roughly EUR 10B remaining at ~EUR 1,700-1,900 retires ~5.5M shares, net of small dilution. I do not use MarketScreener's implied ~357M (NI EUR 24.4B / EPS EUR 68.32), which looks internally inconsistent with the size of the buyback; that is why its EUR 68.3 EPS is above my gross EUR 62.7.

Gross = EUR 65.0B x 36.5% / 378M = EUR 62.7. Haircut for MATCH: 35% x ~10% EPS hit = 3.5%, giving EUR 60.5. I cut the enactment odds from 40% to 35%: Senate cloture failed 50-46 on 07-14 over the Iran-war dispute (sources 23, 24), S.4281 has had no Banking markup (source 26), and the Dutch PM is pushing for a negotiated deal (source 17). I do not go lower, because a December four-corners conference can carry the text without a Senate floor vote (source 23). The result sits inside the EUR 53-68 consensus spread, near its middle on a consistent share count.

Today: ~33x blended NTM EUR 48.4 and ~30.5x 2027 (MarketScreener). NTM EV/EBITDA of 23.6x against a 24.9x 10-year mean (Torre, source 16, a single newsletter, so I use it only as a cross-check). The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 and most participants see one more hike (source 22), so the horizon multiple should not sit above the middle of ASML's mid-20s to mid-30s range. In Oct-2027 the market will also be pricing decelerating growth (+19% in 2028 against +27% in 2027, source 21). I therefore trim 28x to 27.5x.
Twelve Data close on 2026-10-01 (the supervisor's verified rate); 1 ADR = 1 ordinary share.

History is 115-120% (FY24-25, 20-F; source 10), helped by down payments, with contract liabilities of EUR 18.2B. But H1-26 FCF was ~-EUR 1.3B on the receivables build (source 3), and consensus FCF/NI is only ~86% for 2027 and ~84% for 2028 (source 21), which reflects capacity capex for the +30% steps. I cut 95% to 90%, between consensus and history.
Same as in the P/E method.

Torre gives the trailing FCF yield as 1.8% against a 10-year average of 2.6% (source 16). In round 1, 3.25% two-year-forward equalled ~2.7% NTM at the horizon. I add ~10bp for the 2026-09-16 hike cycle (source 22). Cross-check: consensus 2028 FCF of EUR 20.5B (source 21) over today's market cap of ~EUR 615B is ~3.3%.

bear.story: A December FY27 NDAA conference text carries the MATCH Act without a Dutch carve-out, so immersion DUV sales and servicing at five Chinese fabs stop after the 150-day window (China ~20% of FY26 sales). Separately or together, memory pricing rolls over in H2-27 or AI capex digests, the Fed keeps hiking, and 2027 is priced as the peak. GM stalls at 54-55%. The stock de-rates to ~21x a trimmed 2027 EPS of ~EUR 50. The 7% one-day fall on 2026-09-14 shows how quickly sentiment can move this.

base.story: 2027 delivers ~85 low-NA units and sales near the EUR 54.6B consensus, for EPS of ~EUR 52. The June 2027 CMD confirms the 2028 capacity step and supports sales near the EUR 65B consensus. China ends in a narrower negotiated US-Dutch arrangement. With rates higher after the 2026 hikes, the multiple compresses to ~27-28x NTM EPS of ~EUR 58-59.

bull.story: Customers keep pulling forward: TSMC's next-three-year capex steps up sharply, Micron and SK hynix add 2028 capacity, and ASML confirms a further ~30% capacity step for 2028 with better pricing, putting 2028 EPS toward EUR 66-68 (MarketScreener's top end). The MATCH Act dies in conference. The multiple holds at ~31x despite the Fed.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $1,150 the stock trades at ~19.8x 2027 consensus EPS (EUR 51.7 = $58.1) and ~17.5x my Oct-2027 NTM EPS ($65.5). That is 27% below the sentiment-only close of $1,575.15 on 2026-09-14 and below the March-2026 low. Higher rates alone would justify perhaps 25x, not 18x, so trading there would most likely mean one of three things: an absolute cut to 2027 shipments or EUV slot push-outs (contradicting 'close to fully covered'), a TSMC, memory or hyperscaler capex freeze shown in the January 2027 guide, or a December NDAA that enacts the MATCH servicing ban and also hits the China installed base.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor confirmed my primary-document numbers (EUR consensus, contract liabilities, H1 FCF) and flagged three gaps, which I checked. (1) Rates: the FOMC statement (source 22) confirms the 2026-09-16 hike to 3.75-4.00% (12-0) with most participants expecting another. My multiple goes from 28x to 27.5x and my 2028E FCF yield from 3.25% to 3.35%. I keep the trim modest because the NTM EV/EBITDA is already near its 10-year mean. (2) The 2028 earnings base is now built bottom-up from MarketScreener's EUR 65.0B sales consensus at a 36.5% margin on ~378M shares, for a gross EUR 62.7. Consensus FCF conversion of ~84-86% also led me to cut my conversion from 95% to 90%. (3) NDAA timing: ndaa.ai and Bits&Chips confirm cloture failed on 07-14, the Senate returns the week of 11-09, and a December four-corners conference is the path. S.4281 has had no committee markup. I cut MATCH enactment odds from 40% to 35% and the haircut from 4% to 3.5%, and moved the catalyst to December. Net effect: fair value falls from $1,912 to $1,813, about flat to spot. The FCF leg drops most (conversion), and the P/E leg barely moves. I end slightly below the supervisor's $1,880 because I apply consensus FCF conversion and a consistent share count. I do not take MarketScreener's EUR 68.3 2028 EPS at face value, since its implied ~357M shares does not fit a EUR 12B buyback. The ladder is a mixture. The main mode (78%) has a median of $1,940 and sigma 0.33. A bear mode (22%) has a median of $1,240 and sigma 0.30, for MATCH enactment or a cycle-top de-rating like past 40-50% semicap drawdowns. That gives P(>= spot) of 0.48, a median of ~$1,770, a mean of ~$1,883 (consistent with the scenario mean of ~$1,882), and a width in line with 46% realised vol. Analyst targets, as evidence only: MarketScreener mean EUR 2,045, Alpha Spread EUR 2,098; Morgan Stanley EUR 1,700. The 1-month ladder stays near symmetric with 14% sigma: Q3 on 10-14 is the only large scheduled event and MATCH cannot land in the window. Research was limited to 7 follow-up queries; CNBC returned 403, so the FOMC statement came via the Atlanta Fed.
